summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood Private (VPC) deployment for Lumen Health production workloads. Main concerns: VPC peering vs private endpoints, cross-account networking, region restrictions for data residency, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and migration path from Hosted/Dedicated. AE + SE presented high-level topology options and next steps to share diagrams, security docs and sizing.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), David Park (CTO, Lumen Health), Rita Gomez (Lead Infra Eng), Samir Patel (Security Architect), Nina Torres (PM)

Summary: quick discovery focused on private VPC networking options, compliance, and regional constraints.

00:00 Marcus Lee: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, um i'm marcus from redwood inference, this is priya our solutions engineer. quick round robin?
00:08 David Park: david here, CTO, thanks marcus. we're evaluating options to run inference on sensitive PHI-adjacent transcripts so privacy and region controls are the big items.
00:16 Rita Gomez: hi, rita, infra. we own networking and deployment. our ask is we need a private deployment — no internet egress from the model hosts and audit trails.
00:25 Samir Patel: samir, security. SOC2 is necessary and KMS integration is must, ideally HSM-backed keys for long term.
00:33 Marcus Lee: totally, that's why private VPC is a fit. high-level we have two common patterns: either VPC peering between customer VPC and redwood-managed VPC, or private endpoints (AWS privatelink-style) with no peering. each has tradeoffs — want me or priya to run through both?
00:47 Priya Nair: i'll start — VPC peering gives routable IPs and lower latency, but requires careful route table management and cross-account peering setup. privatelink / interface endpoints mean we expose an endpoint service in our account and you create interface endpoints in yours, traffic stays private but it's not routable the same way for health-checks and debug.
01:10 Rita Gomez: what's the limit on connections for privatelink — we have multiple accounts across business units, would we need an endpoint in each account or can we transit through a central VPC?
01:20 Priya Nair: generally you'd put an endpoint per account or use a transit VPC pattern. privatelink is per AZ and per subnet, so you plan endpoints where your traffic originates. for cross-region, privatelink is regional; peering can be cross-region but you pay cross-region data fees and need to consider latency.
01:40 David Park: we need EU data residency for some workloads — do you support deploying the private control plane in eu-west-1 and having the inference hosts there entirely?
01:50 Marcus Lee: yes — Redwood Private can be deployed in the region you own, we support region-constrained deployments. for managed private we run the control plane with customer-managed networking, but if you want full on-prem or air-gapped, we also have an on-prem package.
02:05 Samir Patel: on KMS — can we bring our own KMS/HSM? we require BYOK and key usage policies so no plaintext keys leave our env.
02:13 Priya Nair: BYOK is supported; we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and we have an HSM integration path for dedicated customers. we'll share the HSM onboarding doc but usually it's a combination of envelope encryption and customer-managed CMKs.
02:27 Nina Torres: and audit logs? retention policies? we need 7 years for certain audit trails.
02:33 Marcus Lee: we can provide audit logs from the control plane — request/response metadata, auth events, and model versioning actions. retention is configurable and an add-on for longer retention windows. i'll attach the audit log schema.
02:46 Rita Gomez: networking ops detail: NAT? egress rules? our constraint is zero public egress from model subnets. how do you handle OS and security patch updates on hosts if there's no internet egress?
03:00 Priya Nair: common approaches: we either route egress through customer-managed NAT/proxy so updates pull through your infrastructure, or we push updates via an internal update mirror that you host. for fully air-gapped we do staged images that you import. we'll include options in the doc.
03:18 Samir Patel: ok, so two things — one we need IP allowlisting for our internal callers, two we need mTLS between our appl tier and your endpoints.
03:26 Marcus Lee: yes we support IP allowlists and mutual TLS. for private endpoints it's TLS + AWS security groups — mTLS is supported for Dedicated/Private with client certs.
03:36 David Park: what about load — we expect bursty traffic, maybe 100 to 200 concurrent rps at peak, average 30k tokens/day. what's sizing look like?
03:49 Priya Nair: rough quickball: for that profile we would recommend a small fleet of T4/8 equivalent nodes for cost-optimized, or larger A100/4 for latency-sensitive. dedicated gives fixed throughput; private on your VPC can be right-sized similarly. i'll draft a sizing sheet in the follow-up.
04:05 Rita Gomez: can we start on hosted for dev and then migrate to private for prod? what's the migration path?
04:12 Marcus Lee: absolutely — typical path is hosted for dev/proof-of-concept, then either open a Dedicated reservation or move to Private. we support model version pinning so you can keep behavior consistent. also we provide routing policies so traffic can failover to hosted in emergencies if you allow that.
04:29 Samir Patel: do you provide SLA on private? and what about certifications — SOC2, iso?
04:36 Marcus Lee: Dedicated and Private customers can have enterprise SLAs. Redwood is SOC2 Type II — we'll send the compliance pack; for Private we can include interface options to support your audit.
04:45 Nina Torres: any precedent in healthcare? references?
04:49 Marcus Lee: yes, we've done private deployments with several health customers — i'll include references and anonymized case notes in the pack.
04:56 Rita Gomez: operationally, who owns the model weights in private? are they stored in our S3 or your storage?
05:03 Priya Nair: there are options: you can host weights in customer-managed storage with the compute in your VPC mounting that storage, or we can host the artifacts but encrypt with your KMS. for strict data residency we typically recommend customer-hosted artifacts.
05:18 David Park: pricing — give me a sense. we need a delta vs hosted because procurement will push back.
05:25 Marcus Lee: quickframe — hosted is pay-as-you-go per token. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits (cost-effective for predictable workloads). Private has platform fee + infra + ops and is higher initial but gives isolation and compliance. priya will draft a cost comparison for your estimated volume.
05:40 Samir Patel: regarding network topology, if we do VPC peering we need route propagation into our on-prem. can your engineers partner with ours on the peering and BGP?
05:50 Priya Nair: yes, for Private deployments we do a joint runbook and we can do BGP/Direct Connect support depending on provider. we'll include a sample runbook.
06:03 Rita Gomez: one more question — our infra team wants to limit egress across AZ in case of failover; how do you manage state and model KV caches?
06:14 Priya Nair: runtime keeps KV cache local to instance for latency; for multi-AZ replication we do asynchronous state syncs but prefer stateless scaling with cold-start KV syncing. we'll note replication patterns in the doc — many customers keep caching regional to control egress.
06:32 David Park: ok, sounds good. can you also show latency measurements from eu-west-1 to your nodes if you have public benchmarks?
06:40 Marcus Lee: yes we'll include our regional latency/throughput benchmark deck — they include p95 numbers for common model families.
06:48 Nina Torres: next steps recap?
06:52 Marcus Lee: yes recap: we'll send the security/compliance pack, private VPC topology doc with peering and privatelink patterns, sizing and preliminary cost delta, and schedule a technical deep dive for next week. rita you'll share VPC CIDRs and region constraints. any other items?
07:09 Rita Gomez: i'll send CIDRs and point of contact for peering.
07:13 Samir Patel: i'll send required KMS/HSM controls list.
07:16 Marcus Lee: perfect — thanks all. we'll follow up via email and add a calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
07:22 End of call

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR artifacts (KV cash, privatelink spelled as private link in some segments). There was a short overlap at 03:00 where two speakers spoke simultaneously.
